notes.general_comments: The June 2025 Listening paper consisted of 37 multiple-choice questions. Candidates overall performed well in this paper and most attempted all questions. Candidates should take care when they transf er their answers onto the answer sheet and shade one letter only f or Questions 1 to 34, and two letters f or Questions 35 to 37. The French extracts heard by candidates gradually increased in terms of length and complexity and featured simple transactional exchanges, short monologues, conversations, and interviews. The emphasis of the questions moved from assessing the candidates’ ability to identif y inf ormation contained in short f actual pieces to testing their ability to understand specific information, descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, and explanations in longer extracts. The paper dif f erentiated well.

Some candidates incorrectly chose distractor B, although Arthur said that there were f ew older people amongst their clients. In Question 23, over half the candidates chose the correct answer B. The other candidates heard problèmes, which ref erred to Sylvain’s boss not Sylvain, and incorrectly chose distractor B. The most frequent incorrect answers were distractor B and option C, although there was no mention of comportement positif in the passage. In Question 33, half the cohort successf ully chose B. Nearly a third heard confiance and incorrectly chose distractor A, although Joanne said that she had always been conf ident. notes.35-37: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview with Pierre, an oceanographer in Nouméa in New Caledonia. For each question in this exercise, candidates had to identify two correct statements f rom a choice of f ive. This was an appropriately demanding and challenging exercise at this stage of the paper. Question 35 was attempted well: over three quarters of the candidates successfully selected C and over half chose D. Distractor E was the most common incorrect answer: candidates needed to listen caref ully to understand the sequence of events which resulted in Pierre deciding to become an oceanographer. The f inal sentence gave another clue with ce n’était pas un métier auquel je pensais quand j’étais enfant. In Question 36, over two thirds of the cohort correctly selected B and E. Distractor A was a common incorrect mornings in the laboratory, not most of his time. Nearly a quarter of the candidates incorrectly chose distractor C, which contradicted what Pierre said about the development of tourism in the 15 years he had spent there. Question 37 was the most demanding in this exercise. Nearly half the cohort understood j’ai été triste de rater le mariage de ma sœur et le baptême de ma nièce and successf ully selected A. Over a third correctly chose D. Two thirds heard télescope and incorrectly chose distractor E. Here candidates needed to listen caref ully to the verb f orm, je vais bientôt m’acheter, to understand that Pierre does not have a telescope yet. A third heard conférence en Bretagne and incorrectly chose distractor B, which gave the wrong time f or the event.
